8465.text: AQA Synergy: thematic alternative to Trilogy (which we built). Same total content, completely different unit/topic architecture — can't be aliased. Estimated <10% of AQA Combined Science uptake. Low priority.

_general.text: Eduqas doesn't offer Combined Science — no pill, not a gap.
Eduqas doesn't offer GCSE Biology / Chemistry / Physics standalone or combined. No pills for those.

3400QS.text: WJEC Biology: Wales-only ("not available to centres in England"). Welsh-curriculum content baked in. Park with other Wales-only specs.

_general.text: Eduqas doesn't offer GCSE Biology / Chemistry / Physics.

3410QS.text: WJEC Chemistry: Wales-only ("not available to centres in England"). Park.

_general.text: Eduqas doesn't offer GCSE Biology / Chemistry / Physics.

3420QS.text: WJEC Physics: Wales-only ("not available to centres in England"). Park.

_general.text: OCR doesn't offer GCSE Modern Languages — no OCR pill needed.

C800QS.text: Eduqas French: genuine buildable gap. English-market spec, no Wales restrictions.

3800QS.text: WJEC French (NEW Made-for-Wales reform, first awarding 2027): broad/non-prescriptive themes — could PORT from an Eduqas French build (new Supabase row, restructured into WJEC's 4 units, 30% NEA). NOT a zero-content alias because assessment structure differs. Future cohort only — 2026 students don't sit this yet.

_general.text: OCR doesn't offer GCSE Modern Languages.

C820QS.text: Eduqas Spanish: genuine buildable gap. English-market spec, no Wales restrictions.

3820QS.text: WJEC Spanish: "Wales and the World" is 1 of 3 core themes — Welsh-context vocab/dialogues required. NOT aliasable from Eduqas. Park.

_general.text: OCR doesn't offer GCSE Modern Languages. Eduqas offers French and Spanish only — no German spec, so no Eduqas pill for German.

3810QS.text: WJEC German: same "Wales and the World" core theme as Spanish — Welsh content required. NOT aliasable. Park.

C112QS.text: Eduqas Geography B: problem-solving approach, 3 components incl. dedicated Problem Solving Geography paper. Different themes from Geography A (which we built). Genuine separate build ~30–40 lessons. Small market (Eduqas Geography is minority board).

J384.text: OCR Geography B (Geography for Enquiring Minds): enquiry-led, completely different philosophy from OCR A (Geographical Themes, which we built). OCR B is more popular than OCR A in uptake — highest-value gap of the three.

3111QS.text: WJEC Geography: heavily Welsh-baked (mandatory "Distinctive landscapes in Wales" theme, Snowdonia, Welsh coastal case studies). Wales-only spec. Park.

C100QS.text: Eduqas History: WIRED (23 May 2026) — Supabase row history-eduqas activated, 16 pathways / 167 lessons (all British/non-British depths + Period/Thematic Studies). Cross-pathway exclusions captured (1D+2D, 1G+2B, 1H+2A). Picker option-pick UX for 4 lesson combinations TBD; for now /browse/history-eduqas shows all 16 units. Phase 3 content gen in flight.

J411.text: OCR History B (Schools History Project): partnership with the SHP organisation, different topic options and question style from OCR A. Genuine separate build.

3100QS.text: WJEC History: Unit 1 literally "Studies in Depth — Wales and the wider perspective". Mandatory Welsh history (Plas Mawr at Conwy, etc.). Wales-only spec. Park.

C550QS.text: Eduqas PE: standard 2-component structure. PORT job (new Supabase row, restructured units) — content overlap with existing AQA/Edexcel/OCR PE is high (60–70% — anatomy/physiology/training/sport psychology are universal). NOT a zero-content alias. Lower-priority because Eduqas PE is a minority board.

3550QS.text: WJEC PE: Wales-only, mandatory "Welsh perspective" throughout. Park with other Wales-only specs.

8061.text: AQA Short Course (8061): WIRED (20 May 2026). Pure alias of AQA Spec A — same Supabase row, 4 religions × Beliefs only + Theme A + Theme D (which is "Religion, Peace & Conflict" — relettered to "Theme B" in 8061 wording). Wizard board key "AQA Short Course" saves course_type:"short"; reAqaFilter in js/free-user-filters.js skips -practices units. Subject row spec_code updated to "8062 / 8061" so build-status counts both specs as built.

8063.text: AQA Spec B (Catholic-focused): Component 1 = Catholic Christianity in much greater depth than Spec A. Component 2 = perspectives on one other religion, or Textual Studies on Islam/Judaism. Catholic schools only, ~5–10% of AQA RS uptake. Low priority.

J625.text: OCR Religious Studies (Full Course): different structure from AQA/Edexcel/Eduqas. English-market, real ~40–60 lesson build.

J125.text: OCR Short Course: TRUE alias derived from J625 as a subset. Build OCR Full Course (J625) first, then a short-course mode serves J125 from the same content. No new lessons.

C510QS.text: Eduqas Business: 2-component structure (Business Dynamics + Business Considerations). PORT job — new Supabase row with restructured units, but content overlap with existing AQA/Edexcel/OCR Business is high (60–70% — pricing/marketing/finance/motivation/growth are universal GCSE concepts). NOT a zero-content alias. Lower priority — Eduqas Business is a minority board.

3510QS.text: WJEC Business: Wales-only ("not available to centres in England"). "Welsh perspective" required, references to Wales economy and Business Wales. Park with other Wales-only specs.

C510QS.text: Eduqas Business: 2-component structure. PORT job — new Supabase row with restructured units, ~60–70% content overlap with existing builds. NOT a zero-content alias. Lower priority (Eduqas minority board).

_general.text: Neither Eduqas nor WJEC offers GCSE Citizenship Studies — no pills for those, not a gap.

1CS0.text: Edexcel Citizenship: 2 papers, 5 themes (A–E including "Taking citizenship action"). PORT job — citizenship concepts (rights, democracy, law, active citizenship, identity, global community) overlap heavily with our AQA build. Restructure into Edexcel themes, reuse most material. ~30 lessons.

J270.text: OCR Citizenship: 3 components (Citizenship in perspective / in action / Our rights, our society, our world). PORT job — same content reuse logic as Edexcel. Restructure into OCR components. ~30 lessons.

8061.text: AQA Short Course (8061): WIRED (20 May 2026). See Religious Studies notes.

8063.text: AQA Spec B (Catholic-focused): low priority. See Religious Studies notes.

J625.text: OCR Religious Studies (Full Course): real ~40–60 lesson build.

J125.text: OCR Short Course: TRUE alias from OCR Full Course (J625) once built.

_general.text: Built across AQA, Edexcel, Eduqas, OCR (180 lessons, practice-first). Only WJEC remains and is Wales-only with mandatory Welsh thematic content.

3700QS.text: WJEC English Language: "not available to centres in England" (Qualifications Wales-regulated). Spec mandates Wales-themed reading/writing across units and references Welsh Baccalaureate alignment. Genuine Welsh-content requirement, not just regulator branding — cannot alias from Eduqas. Park — no English-cohort demand.

_general.text: Built across AQA, Edexcel, Eduqas, OCR (775 lessons). WJEC remains and is firmly SKIP.

3720QS.text: WJEC English Literature: "not available to centres in England". Compulsory study of the Library of Wales anthology "Poetry 1900–2000: One Hundred Poets from Wales" plus a dedicated "Welsh Writing in English" section. No overlap with AQA/Edexcel/Eduqas/OCR set texts. Park.

_general.text: Built on AQA 8525 and OCR J277. Edexcel and Eduqas are accessible English-regulated specs; WJEC is Wales-only.

1CP1.text: Edexcel CS 1CP1: 2-paper structure (Principles of CS + Application of Computational Thinking, on-screen). Core content (binary, networks, algorithms, programming, ethics) is ~80% identical to AQA/OCR. PORT job — new Supabase row with units restructured to Edexcel's 2-paper layout, heavy reuse of existing lessons. On-screen Paper 2 means practice-format unit needed for programming questions. Medium priority.

C500QS.text: Eduqas CS C500QS: 2-component structure (theory paper + on-screen computational thinking). Ofqual-regulated, accessible in England. Content scope mirrors AQA/OCR. PORT job — new Supabase row, restructured units, ~70–80% reuse from existing builds. Lower priority (Eduqas minority board for CS).

3500QS.text: WJEC CS 3500QS: "not available to centres in England" but academically near-identical to Eduqas C500QS (both WJEC-authored). No mandatory Welsh content — purely a regulator boundary. After Eduqas build lands, WJEC can alias via slugMap (one row, both boards). Until then, park.

_general.text: Built on AQA 8552 only. D&T is ~50% NEA coursework across all boards, so revision content addresses the written paper only. High concept overlap between boards.

1DT0.text: Edexcel D&T 1DT0: 50% written + 50% NEA. Exam content (materials, processes, designers, sustainability, mechanisms) overlaps heavily with AQA 8552. PORT job — new row, restructured units, ~65–70% reuse. NEA can't be revision-supported. Medium priority.

C600QS.text: Eduqas D&T C600QS: Ofqual-regulated, accessible in England. 50/50 exam/NEA. Exam scope parallels AQA. PORT job — new row, restructured units, heavy reuse. Lower priority (Eduqas minority share for D&T).

J310.text: OCR D&T J310: 50% exam (Principles of D&T + Problem Solving in D&T) + 50% NEA. Same underlying material reorganised. PORT job — new row, restructured, ~65–70% reuse from AQA build. Medium priority.

3600QS.text: WJEC D&T 3600QS: spec PDF is actually the WJEC Eduqas joint specification. Wales-regulated but academically identical to Eduqas C600QS. After Eduqas build lands, WJEC can alias via slugMap. No mandatory Welsh content. Park until Eduqas built.

_general.text: Built on AQA 8261 only. Drama is 60% NEA (devising + scripted performance) + 40% written exam on a set play and live theatre evaluation. Revision content focuses on the exam only — set-play analysis transfers between boards but specific play choices vary.

1DR0.text: Edexcel Drama 1DR0: 60% NEA + 40% written paper on one set play + live theatre review. Generic drama theory (genres, practitioners, staging, design elements, evaluating live theatre) overlaps ~60% with AQA build. Set-play list differs (DNA, Blood Brothers, An Inspector Calls). PORT — set-play lessons need fresh writing. Medium priority.

C690QS.text: Eduqas Drama C690QS: Ofqual-regulated, accessible in England. Same 60/40 split. Generic theory reusable; set-play list differs from AQA. PORT job. Lower priority (Eduqas minority share).

J316.text: OCR Drama J316: being WITHDRAWN — final first teach September 2026, final assessment Summer 2028. Not worth building a new row for a sunsetting qualification; cohorts will migrate to AQA/Edexcel/Eduqas. Skip permanently.

3690QS.text: WJEC Drama 3690QS: "not available to centres in England". Welsh-context theatre practitioners and Welsh writing in the recommended set-text/stimulus lists. Park.

8585.text: AQA Food Prep 8585: 50% NEA + 50% written paper. Exam scope (food commodities, principles of nutrition, food science, food safety, food choice, food provenance) is ~80% identical to Eduqas build — same Ofqual subject content rules. PORT job, very heavy reuse. AQA is the dominant board for this subject; HIGH priority port.

_general.text: Built on Eduqas C560QS only. Food is ~50% NEA (investigation + preparation) + ~50% written exam on nutrition, food science, food safety, food provenance. Exam content is statutorily aligned across Ofqual boards — high reuse potential.

J309.text: OCR Food Prep J309: 50% NEA + 50% written paper. Same Ofqual subject content as Eduqas/AQA. PORT job — new row, restructured units, ~75–80% reuse from Eduqas build. Lower priority than AQA.

3560QS.text: WJEC Food and Nutrition 3560QS: "not available to centres in England". Welsh-perspective requirement, Welsh produce, Wales-specific dietary issues. Named differently ("Food and Nutrition" vs "Food Preparation and Nutrition") reflecting a distinct Welsh subject criteria document. Park.

_general.text: Built on AQA 8572 only. Media Studies is product-focused: each spec stipulates a different list of Close Study Products (CSPs) and set texts students MUST analyse, so reuse across boards is limited even though theoretical frameworks overlap.

C680QS.text: Eduqas Media Studies C680QS: 70% exam + 30% NEA. Uses Stuart Hall / Curran-Seaton / Gauntlet frameworks plus its own CSP list (specific newspaper front pages, music videos, magazines). Frameworks overlap ~50% with AQA; CSPs differ. PORT — fresh CSP lesson writing needed. Eduqas is the largest board for Media Studies, HIGH priority.

J200.text: OCR Media Studies J200: 70% exam + 30% NEA. Distinct CSP list. PORT — frameworks reusable, CSP lessons need fresh writing per OCR's stipulated products. Medium priority.

3680QS.text: WJEC Media Studies 3680QS: "not available to centres in England". Related to Eduqas C680QS but separately Wales-regulated, may incorporate Welsh-media examples (S4C, Welsh-language newspapers) in recommended CSPs. Park.

_general.text: Built on AQA 8271 only. Music is ~60% NEA practical (performing + composing) + ~30–40% written listening/appraising exam on Areas of Study. Areas of Study differ in naming between boards but cover similar Western Classical / Pop / World / Film concept areas — moderate exam-content overlap.

1MU0.text: Edexcel Music 1MU0: 30% performing + 30% composing + 40% listening paper. Four Areas of Study (Instrumental Music 1700–1820, Vocal Music, Music for Stage and Screen, Fusions). Each board sets its own anthology of set works — reuse with AQA limited to generic theory. PORT — restructured around Edexcel's 8 set works, ~40–50% reuse. Largest board for Music, HIGH priority.

C660QS.text: Eduqas Music C660QS: Ofqual-regulated, accessible in England. Four Areas of Study (Musical Forms and Devices, Music for Ensemble, Film Music, Popular Music) with different set works to AQA. PORT — restructured around Eduqas set works, ~40–50% reuse. Medium priority.

J536.text: OCR Music J536: Four Areas of Study (Western Classical Tradition 1650–1910, Rhythms of the World, Film Music, Conventions of Pop). PORT — generic theory reusable, set-piece lessons fresh. Medium priority.

3660QS.text: WJEC Music 3660QS: "not available to centres in England". Spec includes Welsh-tradition music as a recommended area (Cerdd Dant, Welsh folk, S4C contemporary Welsh artists). Park.

8182.text: AQA Psychology 8182: two papers — "Cognition and Behaviour" (memory, perception, development, research methods) + "Social Context and Behaviour" (social influence, language/thought/communication, brain & neuropsychology, psychological problems). 100% exam. Full BUILD from scratch — no source builds. AQA is the dominant board, build first.

_general.text: ZERO existing builds. All three accessible specs (AQA, Edexcel, OCR) are genuine BUILD jobs. Psychology has rising GCSE entry numbers — worth prioritising AQA first (largest cohort), then assessing whether Edexcel/OCR can be ported.

1PS0.text: Edexcel Psychology 1PS0: two papers covering similar core topics (development, memory, social influence, brain, psychological problems, research methods). 100% exam. After AQA build lands, this becomes a PORT (60–70% reuse). Rated BUILD now because AQA isn't built yet — re-evaluate post-AQA.

J203.text: OCR Psychology J203: "Studies and Applications in Psychology 1 & 2" — criminal psychology, development, psychological problems, social influence, memory, sleep & dreaming, research methods. 100% exam. Becomes a PORT (~60% overlap) once AQA build exists. Re-evaluate post-AQA.

_general.text: Built on AQA 8382. Edexcel is the only other board offering GCSE Statistics — small subject (~20k entries/year combined).

1ST0.text: Edexcel Statistics 1ST0: 100% exam, two papers, Foundation/Higher tiered. Content (data collection, processing/representing, summary stats, scatter diagrams, time series, probability, hypothesis testing) is ~85% identical to AQA 8382. PORT — new row, restructured units, very heavy reuse. Low absolute priority (small subject) but cheap port.

8136.text: AQA Economics 8136: two papers — "How Markets Work" (economic foundations, resource allocation, markets in action) + "How the Economy Works" (objectives, role of government, international trade). 100% exam. Full BUILD from scratch. AQA is the dominant board — build first.

_general.text: ZERO existing builds. Both accessible specs (AQA, OCR) are genuine BUILD jobs. Eduqas/WJEC don't offer GCSE Economics, so this is a 2-board family only.

J205.text: OCR Economics J205: two papers covering similar Ofqual-mandated content (markets, money/financial markets, role of government, international economy). 100% exam. Becomes a PORT (~70–80% reuse) once AQA build exists. Re-evaluate post-AQA.

_general.text: Single-board GCSE — only Edexcel offers it. Tiny uptake (~2–3k entries/yr UK-wide), dominated by enrichment/extension at strong state schools and a few independents. Heavy physics overlap with existing Separate Sciences Physics builds.

1AS0.text: Edexcel Astronomy 1AS0: two 1h45 written papers — Naked-eye Astronomy + Telescopic Astronomy (50/50, no coursework). PORT — ~40–50% reuses Separate Physics content (gravity, orbits, Hubble's constant, stellar lifecycle, EM spectrum) but needs bespoke units on celestial sphere, lunar/solar motion, telescope optics. Niche audience.

_general.text: Vanishing GCSE — only WJEC Eduqas now offers it (AQA + OCR withdrew). Total UK entries <1k/yr. Eduqas and WJEC specs are the SAME document (jointly accredited). Decent overlap with the Electronics topic in our Physics builds plus systems thinking from D&T AQA.

C490QS.text: Eduqas Electronics C490QS: Component 1 Discovering Electronics (40%) + Component 2 Application of Electronics (40%) + NEA system-realisation task (20%). PORT — circuit theory, logic gates, components overlap with Physics; needs new units on PIC microcontrollers and system design. Tiny audience.

3490QS.text: WJEC Electronics 3490QS: byte-identical spec to Eduqas C490QS — same WJEC Eduqas document, dual-accredited by Ofqual and Qualifications Wales. Pure alias job once C490QS exists — one Supabase row, slugMap aliases both boards. No additional content. No Welsh-perspective rewrite needed.

8852.text: AQA Engineering 8852: 2h written exam (60%) + NEA practical engineering project (40%). Content covers engineering materials, manufacturing processes, mechanical/electronic/electrical/pneumatic systems. PORT — ~50% reuses D&T AQA materials/manufacturing units, supplemented by systems/mechanisms content from Physics. Niche but defensible.

_general.text: AQA 8852 Engineering is the only mainstream written-exam GCSE Engineering — distinct from OCR's Cambridge Nationals Engineering Design (vocational, internally assessed). Entries ~5–7k/yr, mostly UTCs and technical colleges. Significant overlap with our D&T AQA 8552 build.

Single-spec GCSE — only WJEC Eduqas offers it (AQA withdrew years ago). Total UK entries <1k/yr, almost entirely a handful of independent and grammar schools. Eduqas and WJEC versions are the SAME jointly-accredited document.

C180QS.text: Eduqas Geology C180QS: Geological Principles (50% written) + Investigative Geology (50% written, mandatory fieldwork statement but no coursework marks). PORT — tectonics/weathering/water cycle reuses Geography Paper 1; mineralogy/rock chemistry reuses Chemistry; needs new units on stratigraphy, fossils, geological mapping. Tiny audience.

3180QS.text: WJEC Geology 3180QS: byte-identical to Eduqas C180QS — same WJEC Eduqas document, dual-accredited. Pure alias job once C180QS exists. One Supabase row, slugMap aliases both boards. No Welsh-perspective rewrite required.

_general.text: OCR is the SOLE board offering Ancient History at GCSE (J198). No aliasing possible. Small but loyal audience (~3–4k entries/yr), mostly independent and grammar schools. EBacc-recognised. Distinct from Classical Civilisation — source-led study of specific ancient periods/figures.

J198.text: OCR Ancient History J198: two papers — Greece and the Persian Empire + Rome (period studies + depth studies). Heavy ancient-source analysis (Herodotus, Tacitus). Clean ~30–40 lesson build but no reuse from any existing StudyVault subject. Low priority unless an independent-school customer requests.

_general.text: OCR is the SOLE board offering Classical Civilisation (J199). No aliasing possible. ~12–15k entries/yr — biggest of the OCR Classics trio. Studies Greek and Roman literature, art and society in English translation, so accessible to non-classicists. EBacc-recognised.

J199.text: OCR Classical Civilisation J199: two components — Thematic Study (Myth and Religion or War and Warfare) + Literature and Culture (Homeric World or Roman City). All texts in English translation. ~30–40 lesson build, fully original. Most commercially viable of the three OCR Classics specs given larger entry base.

_general.text: OCR is the SOLE board offering Classical Greek (J292). No aliasing possible. Tiny audience (~1–1.5k entries/yr), almost exclusively independent and selective schools. Language-learning spec — grammar, vocabulary, set-text translation. Distinct from Edexcel Modern Greek 1GK0.

J292.text: OCR Classical Greek J292: four components — Language (translation + comprehension), Prose Literature, Verse Literature, Literature/Culture option. Set texts rotate every 2–3 years. Would need a practice-format build similar to MFL pipeline plus heavy set-text annotation. No reuse. Lowest priority of any Classics build.

_general.text: Three GCSE Latin specs across OCR (J282, ~10k entries), Eduqas (C580QS) and WJEC (3580QS). Eduqas and WJEC specs are the IDENTICAL document — "WJEC Eduqas GCSE (9-1) in Latin", dual-designated. Structures across boards are broadly comparable but set texts differ per board and rotate every 2–3 years.

C580QS.text: Eduqas Latin C580QS: three components — Latin Language (translation/comprehension), Latin Literature (verse + prose set texts, rotating biennially), and Roman Civilisation. Larger English-market share than WJEC. Most commercially viable Latin build of the three. Best built first; OCR could then PORT the language-skills core.

J282.text: OCR Latin J282: three components — Language paper, Prose Literature, Verse/Sources/Culture option. Largest entry base of the three Latin specs. If Eduqas Latin built first, language-skills practice unit ports cleanly (grammar and core vocab are identical). Set-text lessons need fresh writes — OCR set texts differ.

3580QS.text: WJEC Latin 3580QS: literally the SAME document as Eduqas C580QS — "WJEC Eduqas GCSE (9-1) in Latin", single dual-coded qualification. If we build Eduqas Latin, WJEC is a true alias via slugMap — one Supabase row, both board labels. No new content.

_general.text: Edexcel is the sole board offering Biblical Hebrew at GCSE (1BH0). Tiny entry base (~200–400/yr), concentrated in Jewish faith schools. Language-and-set-text spec. No cross-board aliasing. No StudyVault adjacency.

1BH0.text: Edexcel Biblical Hebrew 1BH0: Paper 1 Language (translation, comprehension, grammar) + Paper 2 Set Text (prescribed Hebrew Bible passages, rotated every 3 years). Audience too small to justify a build — almost exclusively Jewish faith schools with bespoke in-house resources. Park unless a specific school requests.

_general.text: Edexcel Greek 1GK0 is MODERN Greek (a Modern Foreign Language GCSE), entirely distinct from OCR Classical Greek J292. Sole board for Modern Greek at GCSE. Audience ~1k entries/yr — overwhelmingly heritage speakers.

1GK0.text: Edexcel Modern Greek 1GK0: PIVOTED to exam-technique guide approach (2026-05-20 plan, see arabic/russian/turkish notes). 8–10 article lessons in English on exam structure, translation technique, register, mark-scheme calibration — NOT a full vocab/grammar build. Heritage speakers already speak; what they need is exam-skills coaching. Short Greek examples (sample answers, translation extracts) need a native-speaker spot-check before ship.

_general.text: All three WJEC Welsh specs (Welsh Language, Welsh Literature, Welsh Second Language) are "not available to centres in England" — Qualifications Wales-regulated for Welsh-medium and bilingual schools in Wales. StudyVault targets English-market students. Firm SKIP across the family.

3000CS.text: WJEC Welsh Language 3000CS: first-language Welsh GCSE for Welsh-medium schools, broadly equivalent to AQA English Language. Wales-only — not available to centres in England. StudyVault does not deliver Welsh-medium content. Permanently skip.

3010CS.text: WJEC Welsh Literature 3010CS: set-text literature GCSE taught entirely through the medium of Welsh — novels, drama and poetry by Welsh-language authors. Wales-only. No StudyVault audience, no realistic content reuse. Permanently skip.

3020CS.text: WJEC Welsh Second Language 3020CS: four-skills MFL-style GCSE in Welsh for non-Welsh-medium pupils in Wales. Architecturally similar to MFL practice builds, but zero English-market demand. Permanently skip.

_general.text: Wales operates a unique double-GCSE maths structure: every pupil sits TWO separate GCSEs — Mathematics (3300QS) AND Mathematics-Numeracy (3310QS) — both Wales-only, both "not available to centres in England". ~30k entries/yr each. Distinct from English-market Eduqas Mathematics (single GCSE).

3300QS.text: WJEC Mathematics 3300QS: Wales-only GCSE, paired with Mathematics-Numeracy 3310QS as a Welsh double-maths award. Content overlaps with Eduqas Mathematics but assessment structure and tier boundaries differ, and regulated by Welsh Government with no access for English centres. Park.

1AA0.text: Edexcel Arabic 1AA0: NEW PLAN (2026-05-20) — exam-technique guide, not full MFL build. ~8-10 article lessons in English covering paper structure, translation technique (MSA vs dialectal awareness), register, mark-scheme calibration. Short Arabic extracts (sample answers, set phrases) need native-speaker spot-check — script handling (harakat / vowel pointing) is the main risk on unfamiliar words. Heritage-speaker audience (faith schools, supplementary schools).

8638.text: AQA Bengali 8638: NEW PLAN (2026-05-20) — exam-technique guide approach. ~8-10 article lessons in English. Bengali script extracts need native-speaker review before ship (Tier 3 language for my confidence). Heritage-speaker audience (Bengali diaspora in a few UK cities). Lower priority than higher-uptake languages.

8673.text: AQA Chinese (Spoken Mandarin) 8673: speaking-only variant. Exam-technique guide focuses on the speaking/listening papers — role play, photo card, conversation strategy. ~6-8 lessons (smaller than the full-skills variant because no reading/writing paper). Native ear on the pinyin/tone examples.

_general.text: NEW PLAN (2026-05-20): exam-technique guide approach for both Chinese variants. Heritage speakers + Mandarin learners need exam-skills coaching more than vocab building. Native-speaker review of any tone marks and short character extracts mandatory before ship (Tier 2 for me — tones are my weak spot).

1CN0.text: Edexcel Chinese (Mandarin or Cantonese) 1CN0: full 4-paper spec. Exam-technique guide ~8-10 lessons covering character recognition strategy, translation technique, formal vs colloquial register. More mainstream than the AQA spoken-only variant.

1GU0.text: Edexcel Gujarati 1GU0: NEW PLAN (2026-05-20) — exam-technique guide approach. Heritage-speaker cohort (Gujarati diaspora, Leicester/London/Bolton supplementary schools). ~8-10 article lessons in English. Gujarati script extracts need native-speaker review (Tier 3 for me). Low priority unless a partner school requests.

8678.text: AQA Modern Hebrew 8678: NEW PLAN (2026-05-20) — exam-technique guide. ~8-10 article lessons in English on paper structure, translation technique, register issues. RTL script handling for any short Hebrew extracts. Native-speaker spot-check on niqqud (vowel pointing) for unfamiliar words. Very small audience (~500 entries nationally, Jewish faith schools).

8633.text: AQA Italian 8633: full standard MFL spec (4 papers, F/H, three AQA themes, grammar/vocab lists). PORT from existing French/German/Spanish AQA practice builds is very high reuse — same factory, same input types, same theme structure; only vocabulary and example sentences need Italian. Highest-value port in this cluster.

_general.text: Italian is the largest minority MFL in UK schools and the strongest cross-board uptake of any community-language family. AQA + Edexcel only. EXCEPTION to the heritage-language exam-technique-guide plan — Italian gets the full MFL practice build (Tier 1 confidence, mixed heritage + learner audience).

1IN0.text: Edexcel Italian 1IN0: standard 4-skills/4-papers F/H. PORT from existing Edexcel French/German/Spanish builds — factory and theme structure align directly; Italian vocab and audio only. Pair with AQA 8633 to cover both boards efficiently.

1JA0.text: Edexcel Japanese 1JA0: NEW PLAN (2026-05-20) — exam-technique guide. ~8-10 article lessons in English on paper structure, translation technique, register (formal vs casual), kanji vs kana usage strategy. Short Japanese extracts (sample answers) need native-speaker spot-check, especially honorifics and tone (Tier 2 for me). Motivated audience (state-school enrichment + Saturday schools).

8683.text: AQA Panjabi 8683: NEW PLAN (2026-05-20) — exam-technique guide approach. Heritage-speaker cohort (Sikh community in West Midlands/Slough/Southall). ~8-10 article lessons in English. Gurmukhi script extracts need native-speaker review (Tier 3 for me). Build only on direct school demand.

1PN0.text: Edexcel Persian 1PN0: NEW PLAN (2026-05-20) — exam-technique guide. ~8-10 article lessons in English. RTL/Nastaliq-style script extracts need native-speaker review (Tier 3 for me). Iranian-diaspora heritage audience. Low priority unless a partner school requests.

8688.text: AQA Polish 8688: NEW PLAN (2026-05-20) — exam-technique guide approach. Polish is the most-spoken non-English first language in UK schools, so audience is the largest of any heritage-language family. ~8-10 article lessons in English on paper structure, translation technique, register issues common to heritage speakers (case usage, formal vs colloquial). Native-speaker spot-check on Polish extracts (Tier 2 — case endings and idioms are my weak spot). Strong candidate for the heritage-language pilot.

_general.text: Portuguese is one of two heritage-language EXCEPTIONS that keeps the full MFL practice build (Tier 1 confidence due to Romance-language overlap with Spanish, moderate audience).

1PG0.text: Edexcel Portuguese 1PG0: standard 4-skills/4-papers F/H. PORT from MFL factory — engine and theme structure reuse cleanly with Spanish (similar Romance structure); Portuguese vocab/audio only. Heritage-speaker audience (Portuguese and Brazilian-Portuguese communities, predominantly London). Moderate priority.

1RU0.text: Edexcel Russian 1RU0: NEW PLAN (2026-05-20) — exam-technique guide approach. ~8-10 article lessons in English on paper structure, translation technique (both directions), register, mark-scheme calibration. Short Russian extracts (sample answers, Cyrillic) need native-speaker spot-check (Tier 2 for me — case usage and idioms). NOMINATED PILOT for the heritage-language exam-technique-guide approach: reasonable audience, my content level for English-heavy framing is solid, Edexcel-only spec keeps wiring simple.

1TU0.text: Edexcel Turkish 1TU0: NEW PLAN (2026-05-20) — exam-technique guide. ~8-10 article lessons in English. Turkish uses Latin script with diacritics, so script handling is straightforward. Native-speaker spot-check on Turkish extracts (Tier 2 for me). Heritage-speaker audience (Turkish/Cypriot communities, North London).

8648.text: AQA Urdu 8648: ~8-10 article lessons in English on paper structure, translation technique, register issues. Nastaliq RTL script extracts need native-speaker review (Tier 3 for me). Reasonable cohort — strong candidate after Russian pilot lands.

_general.text: NEW PLAN (2026-05-20): exam-technique guide approach, not full MFL build. Heritage-speaker audience (Birmingham, Bradford, East London). Both boards covered.

1UR0.text: Edexcel Urdu 1UR0: same exam-technique-guide plan as AQA 8648, adapted to Edexcel paper structure. Build paired with AQA version once template is proven.

_general.text: OCR-only Cambridge National. Three units: R057 (externally assessed exam, 40%) + R058 + R059 (NEA portfolio, 60%). Small cohort, commonly run in academies/UTCs. R057 has genuine revisable content (child health, nutrition).

J809.text: OCR J809: Real build needed but only R057 (40% exam) is genuinely revision-worthy — child health and well-being. R058/R059 are portfolio-only (skip from revision scope). Recommend ~10–12 lessons covering R057. Lower priority than core GCSE backlog.

_general.text: OCR-only. Unity has a bespoke build (23 lessons) but Unity content was made with Unity-specific teacher resources baked in — NOT portable to free tier. Free-tier needs a fresh generic build.

J834.text: OCR J834: Fresh BUILD needed (Unity content can't port — built around Unity teacher resources). R093 (externally assessed unit) is the revision-relevant focus; NEA units R094–R099 are portfolio so light coverage only. OCR-only, no aliasing possible. Mid priority.

_general.text: OCR-only. R038 (externally assessed) + R039 + R040 (NEA — CAD modelling, design work). Heavy CAD/portfolio bias; revision applies only to R038. Small UTC/technical-college cohort.

J822.text: OCR J822: Park. Small cohort (mostly UTCs/technical academies) and only R038 has revision value — R039/R040 are CAD coursework. Revision-content moat thin against build cost. Revisit only if a school directly requests.

_general.text: OCR-only. R014 written + R015 + R016 NEA (manual + CAM manufacturing). Very small cohort, workshop-dependent. Revisable content limited to R014.
